title: EPA Envirofacts and ECHO (TRI, GHGRP, SDWIS, Superfund, compliance and enforcement)
questions: largest greenhouse gas emitters in a state
Superfund sites on the National Priorities List in a state
drinking water violations in a state
EPA enforcement cases and penalties under the Clean Air Act in a state

manual.how: Open each link in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md in a browser: Envirofacts links return CSV pages of 5,000 rows; ECHO links take two steps (the first returns a QueryID, then open the get_qid link with it). Save each file under the name shown and upload. Without the links: Envirofacts at https://enviro.epa.gov (search, then download CSV); ECHO at https://echo.epa.gov/facilities/facility-search and https://echo.epa.gov/facilities/enforcement-case-search (Download Data); TRI and GHGRP full-year files at https://www.epa.gov/toxics-release-inventory-tri-program/tri-basic-data-files-calendar-years-1987-present and https://www.epa.gov/ghgreporting/data-sets.

cache.why: ECHO refreshes weekly and SDWIS quarterly; data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: EPA data are U.S. government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105; https://www.epa.gov/web-policies-and-procedures/epa-disclaimers); cite EPA and do not imply endorsement.

citation: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, {dataset}, Envirofacts (data.epa.gov) / ECHO (echo.epa.gov), retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Which reporting year? TRI and GHGRP publish one year at a time with a lag of about 10 months; say the year used.
Facilities or emissions? GHGRP rows are facility x gas x year; sum CO2e over gases for facility totals.
